# Fascia Of The Neck & Posterior Triangle Till Last 4 CN

**1. Mention tributaries of the external jugular vein (EJV)**  
- Anterior jugular vein  
- Transverse cervical vein  
- Suprascapular vein  
- Posterior external jugular vein  

**2. Which lymph nodes accompany the EJV? What is its clinical importance?**  
- Superficial cervical lymph nodes  
- Acts as a venous manometer in clinical settings  

**3. Investing layer of deep cervical fascia encloses which muscles, glands, and spaces?**  
- Muscles: Sternocleidomastoid, Trapezius  
- Glands: Parotid, Submandibular  
- Spaces: Supraclavicular, Suprasternal  

**4. Describe the superior attachment of the investing layer of deep fascia**  
- External occipital protuberance  
- Superior nuchal line  
- Mastoid process  
- Base of mandible  

**5. Describe the inferior attachment of the investing layer of deep fascia**  
- Spine of scapula  
- Acromion  
- Clavicle  
- Manubrium  

**6. Describe the attachments of the prevertebral fascia**  
- Superior: Base of skull  
- Inferior: Extends into superior mediastinum up to anterior longitudinal ligament of T3–T4  
- Laterally: Deficient below trapezius  
- Anteriorly: Separated from pharynx by retropharyngeal space  

**7. Describe relations of the prevertebral fascia**  
- Behind: Prevertebral & scalene muscles, brachial & cervical plexus, subclavian artery  
- In front: Pharynx, larynx, oesophagus, trachea, carotid sheath, sympathetic chain, subclavian vein  

**8. Describe attachments of the pretracheal fascia**  
- Superior: Hyoid bone, oblique line of thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage  
- Inferior: Descends into thorax enclosing thyroid veins, infrahyoid muscles, blends with adventitia of aortic arch & fibrous pericardium  

**9. What surrounds the brachial plexus and subclavian artery?**  
- Axillary sheath  

**10. Neck infection behind the prevertebral fascia may spread how?**  
- Forward, pushing pharyngeal wall  
- Laterally into posterior triangle  
- Inferiorly into superior mediastinum  

**11. Neck infection in front of pretracheal fascia may extend to where?**  
- Anterior mediastinum / suprasternal area  

**12. Neck infection in front of prevertebral fascia extends to where?**  
- Posterior mediastinum  

**13. Retropharyngeal space is closed superiorly by what, laterally by what, and opens inferiorly into where?**  
- Superiorly: Base of skull  
- Laterally: Carotid sheath  
- Inferiorly: Superior mediastinum  

**14. Mention contents of the carotid sheath**  
- Common carotid artery / Internal carotid artery (medial)  
- Internal jugular vein (lateral)  
- Vagus nerve (posterior, between them)  

**15. What lies in front of the carotid sheath and what lies behind it?**  
- In front: Ansa cervicalis  
- Behind: Sympathetic trunk  

**16. Which lymph nodes lie along the carotid sheath?**  
- Deep cervical lymph nodes  

**17. Describe origin and insertion of sternocleidomastoid muscle**  
- Origin:  
  - Sternal head: Superolateral part of anterior surface of manubrium  
  - Clavicular head: Medial one‑third of clavicle  
- Insertion: Mastoid process and lateral one‑third of superior nuchal line  

**18. Describe nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid muscle**  
- Motor: Spinal accessory nerve  
- Sensory (proprioception): Ventral rami of C2 and C3  

**19. Mention relations of sternocleidomastoid muscle**  
- Covered by skin and superficial fascia containing platysma, EJV, great auricular, transverse cervical, medial supraclavicular nerves, superficial cervical lymph nodes  
- Deep fascia  

**20. Describe actions of sternocleidomastoid muscle**  
- One side: Tilts head to same side and rotates face to opposite side  
- Both sides: Flex neck  
- Acts as accessory muscle of inspiration  

**21. Describe roof and floor of posterior triangle of neck**  
- Roof: Skin, superficial fascia, investing layer of deep cervical fascia  
- Floor: Prevertebral fascia and muscles (semispinalis capitis, splenius capitis, levator scapulae, scalenus medius, scalenus anterior)  

**22. Superior and inferior parts of posterior triangle are called what and divided by what?**  
- Superior: Occipital triangle  
- Inferior: Supraclavicular triangle  
- Divided by: Inferior belly of omohyoid  

**23. Mention nerves in posterior triangle of neck**  
- Spinal accessory nerve  
- Roots and trunks of brachial plexus  
- Cutaneous branches of cervical plexus  
- Muscular branches  

**24. Mention vessels of posterior triangle of neck**  
- Third part of subclavian artery  
- Subclavian vein  
- Suprascapular artery and vein  
- Transverse cervical artery and vein  
- External jugular vein  
- Occipital artery  

**25. Mention cutaneous branches of cervical plexus with root values**  
- Lesser occipital (C2)  
- Great auricular (C2, C3)  
- Transverse cervical (C2, C3)  
- Supraclavicular (C3, C4)  

**26. Roots and trunks of brachial plexus lie between which muscles and with which artery?**  
- Between scalenus anterior and scalenus medius  
- With subclavian artery  

**27. Third part of subclavian artery is separated from vein by what?**  
- Scalenus anterior muscle  

**28. Mention branches of third part of subclavian artery**  
- Deep branch of transverse cervical artery (in ~65%)  

**29. Suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries arise from what and from which part?**  
- Thyrocervical trunk  
- First part of subclavian artery  

**30. Transverse cervical artery passes deep to which muscle?**  
- Trapezius  

**31. Lymph drainage of posterior triangle: lower part drains to where, upper part to where?**  
- Lower part: Supraclavicular nodes  
- Upper part: Occipital nodes  

**32. Describe superior border of anterior triangle**  
- Inferior border of mandible  
- Line joining angle of mandible to mastoid process  

**33. Mention bounds of submental triangle**  
- Base: Body of hyoid bone  
- Sides: Anterior bellies of digastric  
- Apex: Symphysis menti  
- Floor: Mylohyoid muscles  

**34. Mention contents of submental triangle**  
- Submental lymph nodes  
- Submental artery and vein  
- Mylohyoid nerve and vessels  
- Small veins forming anterior jugular vein  

**35. Mention bounds of digastric (submandibular) triangle**  
- Anterior: Anterior belly of digastric  
- Posterior: Posterior belly of digastric & stylohyoid  
- Base: Inferior border of mandible  
- Floor: Mylohyoid & hyoglossus  
- Roof: Skin, superficial fascia, deep fascia  

**36. Mention contents of anterior part of digastric triangle**  
- Submandibular gland and lymph nodes  
- Facial vein (superficial), facial artery (deep)  
- Mylohyoid nerve and vessels  
- Submandibular duct, ganglion, lingual and hypoglossal nerves  

**37. Mention contents of posterior part of digastric triangle**  
- Lower part of parotid gland  
- External carotid artery  
- Carotid sheath and contents  

**38. Mention bounds of carotid triangle**  
- Superior: Posterior belly of digastric  
- Anterior: Superior belly of omohyoid  
- Posterior: Anterior border of SCM  
- Floor: Hyoglossus, thyrohyoid, and pharyngeal constrictors  

**39. Mention arterial contents of carotid triangle**  
- Common carotid artery  
- Internal carotid artery  
- External carotid artery and its branches  
- Carotid sinus and body  

**40. Mention veins and lymph nodes of carotid triangle**  
- Internal jugular vein  
- Tributaries: pharyngeal, lingual, common facial, superior thyroid veins  

**41. Mention nerves of carotid triangle**  
- Cranial nerves IX, X, XI  
- Ansa cervicalis  
- Sympathetic chain  

**42. Mention bounds of muscular triangle**  
- Anterior: Midline of neck  
- Posterosuperior: Superior belly of omohyoid  
- Posteroinferior: Anterior border of SCM  
- Floor: Pretracheal fascia  

**43. Describe origin and insertion of sternohyoid and sternothyroid muscles**  
- Sternohyoid: O: back of manubrium & medial end of clavicle; I: lower border of hyoid bone  
- Sternothyroid: O: back of manubrium & first costal cartilage; I: oblique line of thyroid cartilage  

**44. Describe origin and insertion of thyrohyoid and omohyoid muscles**  
- Thyrohyoid: O: oblique line of thyroid cartilage; I: lower border of hyoid body & greater cornu  
- Omohyoid:  
  - Superior belly: O: lower border of hyoid body;  
  - Inferior belly: O: upper border of scapula & suprascapular ligament;  
  - I: intermediate tendon held by fascial sling attached to clavicle  

**45. Describe nerve supply of infrahyoid muscles**  
- All supplied by ansa cervicalis except thyrohyoid: C1 fibres via hypoglossal nerve  

**46. Describe movements of infrahyoid muscles**  
- All: Depress larynx (except thyrohyoid which elevates or depresses)  
- Sternohyoid: Depresses hyoid after swallowing  
- Sternothyroid: Depresses larynx after swallowing  
- Thyrohyoid: Depresses hyoid or elevates larynx  
- Omohyoid: Depresses hyoid, tenses deep cervical fascia during inspiration  

**47. Describe origin, insertion, and nerve supply of digastric and stylohyoid muscles**  
- Digastric:  
  - O: Anterior belly – digastric fossa of mandible; Posterior belly – mastoid notch of temporal bone  
  - I: Intermediate tendon to hyoid  
  - N: Anterior belly – mylohyoid nerve (V3); Posterior belly – facial nerve (VII)  
- Stylohyoid: O: posterior surface of styloid process; I: hyoid at tendon pierced by posterior belly of digastric; N: facial nerve (VII)  

**48. Describe origin, insertion, and nerve supply of mylohyoid and geniohyoid muscles**  
- Mylohyoid: O: mylohyoid line of mandible; I: anterior fibres into mylohyoid raphe, posterior fibres into hyoid; N: nerve to mylohyoid (V3)  
- Geniohyoid: O: inferior genial tubercle of mandible; I: body of hyoid; N: C1 via hypoglossal nerve  

**49. Describe actions of suprahyoid muscles**  
- Digastric: Depresses mandible if hyoid fixed, elevates hyoid during swallowing  
- Stylohyoid: Elevates hyoid backwards  
- Mylohyoid: Supports floor of mouth, depresses mandible, elevates hyoid in early swallowing  
- Geniohyoid: Elevates hyoid or depresses mandible  

**50. Describe exit of cervical plexus roots from bone**  
- Between anterior and posterior tubercles of cervical transverse processes  

**51. What lies anterior and posterior to cervical plexus?**  
- Anterior: Prevertebral fascia  
- Posterior: Scalenus medius  

**52. Mention communicating branches of cervical plexus**  
- Grey rami from superior cervical ganglion to all roots  
- C1 fibres join hypoglossal nerve  
- C2 to sternocleidomastoid, C2–C4 to trapezius (sensory)  

**53. List muscular branches of cervical plexus**  
- Infrahyoid muscles via ansa cervicalis  
- Prevertebral & scalene muscles  
- Levator scapulae  
- Diaphragm via phrenic nerve  

**54. Describe structure of ansa cervicalis**  
- Superior limb (descending hypoglossi): C1 fibres join hypoglossal nerve, then descend in front of carotid sheath  
- Inferior limb (descending cervicalis): C2–C3 fibres descend in front of IJV, join superior limb  

**55. The sympathetic chain lies between which structures?**  
- Posterior: Prevertebral fascia  
- Anterior: Carotid sheath  

**56. List groups of postganglionic parasympathetic fibres**  
- Group 1: Communicating rami to nearest nerve  
- Group 2: Form plexus around nearest artery  
- Group 3: Visceral branches to nearest viscera  

**57. Fibres connecting middle and inferior cervical ganglia are called?**  
- Ansa subclavia  

**58. Preganglionic fibres from cervical sympathetic chain arise from?**  
- Upper thoracic ganglia  

**59. Largest and smallest cervical ganglia?**  
- Largest: Superior cervical ganglion  
- Smallest: Middle cervical ganglion  

**60. Describe site of each cervical ganglion**  
- Superior: Between ECA & longus capitis at C2–C3  
- Middle: Related to inferior thyroid at C6–C7  
- Inferior: At transverse process of C7 & neck of first rib  

**61. Mention branches of superior cervical ganglion**  
- Communicating branches to upper 4 cervical + lower 4 cranial nerves  
- Vascular plexus around ECA & ICA  
- Visceral: pharyngeal plexus, superior cervical cardiac, thyroid nerves  

**62. Mention branches of middle cervical ganglion**  
- Communicating to C5–C6  
- Ansa subclavia & plexus around inferior thyroid artery  
- Visceral: thyroid plexus, middle cardiac, tracheal & oesophageal branches  

**63. Mention branches of inferior cervical ganglion**  
- Communicating to C7–C8  
- Vascular plexus around vertebral artery  
- Visceral: inferior cervical cardiac to deep cardiac plexus  

**64. CN IX passes between which arteries initially and later?**  
- Initially: IJV & ICA  
- Later: ECA & ICA  

**65. CN IX passes between which muscles?**  
- Superior constrictor & middle constrictor  

**66. CN IX has how many ganglia and exits via which skull foramen?**  
- Two ganglia: superior & inferior  
- Exits via middle part of jugular foramen  

**67. Enumerate branches of CN IX**  
- Tympanic branch  
- Carotid branch (sinus & body)  
- Pharyngeal (shares in pharyngeal plexus)  
- Muscular to stylopharyngeus  
- Tonsillar (tonsil & soft palate)  
- Lingual (posterior 1/3 of tongue & vallate papillae)  

**68. CN IX is tested by?**  
- Gentle tickling of posterior pharyngeal wall  

**69. CN IX is usually affected with which cranial nerve?**  
- CN X  

**70. Describe course of tympanic branch of CN IX**  
- Enters middle ear via tympanic canaliculus  
- Forms tympanic plexus  
- Gives fibres to greater & lesser petrosal nerves for parotid gland  
- Sensory to middle ear mucosa, auditory tube, mastoid air cells  

**71. Cranial accessory nerve joining vagus distributes fibres mainly through?**  
- Pharyngeal & recurrent laryngeal nerves  

**72. Vagus nerve passes initially between which vessels and then between which vessels?**  
- Initially: IJV & ICA  
- Then: IJV & CCA  

**73. Branches of vagus from superior vagal ganglion**  
- Meningeal: Dura of posterior cranial fossa  
- Auricular: Concha, root of auricle, post half of external auditory meatus & tympanic membrane  

**74. Branches of vagus from inferior vagal ganglion**  
- Pharyngeal nerve: to middle constrictor, pharyngeal plexus  
- Superior laryngeal nerve:  
  - External branch: pierces inferior constrictor, supplies cricothyroid  
  - Internal branch: pierces thyrohyoid membrane, mucosa above vocal cords  

**75. Branches of vagus in neck**  
- Carotid nerve to carotid body  
- Cardiac nerves (superior & inferior)  
- Right recurrent laryngeal: loops subclavian, ascends in tracheoesophageal groove with inferior thyroid artery  

**76. Branches of vagus in thorax**  
- Left recurrent laryngeal nerve  
- Pulmonary & cardiac branches  

**77. Results of vagal paralysis**  
- Nasal regurgitation  
- Hoarseness  
- Flattened palatal arches  
- Cadaveric vocal cord position  
- Dysphagia  

**78. Irritation of auricular branch of vagus leads to?**  
- Reflex cough  

**79. In vagal paralysis, uvula deviates to which side?**  
- Opposite side  

**80. Irritation of CN XI leads to?**  
- Torticollis  

**81. Branches of hypoglossal nerve**  
- Group 1: C1 fibres anatomically related to hypoglossal: meningeal branch, geniohyoid, thyrohyoid, descending hypoglossi (ansa cervicalis superior root)  
- Group 2: From hypoglossal itself: styloglossus, genioglossus, hyoglossus, all intrinsic tongue muscles

# Thalamus & Hypothalamus & 3rd Ventricle

**1. Mention the dorsal and ventral parts of the thalamus**  
- **Dorsal part:**  
  - Thalamus  
  - Metathalamus (medial and lateral geniculate bodies)  
  - Epithalamus (pineal body, habenular nuclei, posterior commissure)  
- **Ventral part:**  
  - Hypothalamus  
  - Subthalamus  
- They are divided by the hypothalamic sulcus  

**2. Describe the ends of the thalamus**  
- Anterior end: lies posterior to the interventricular foramen of Monro  
- Posterior end: expanded to form the pulvinar  

**3. Mention the surfaces of the thalamus and their relations**  
- Superior surface: free, related to choroid plexus, forms part of the floor of the lateral ventricle  
- Inferior surface: separated from ventral structures by the hypothalamic sulcus  
- Medial surface: forms lateral wall of the third ventricle; both sides connected by interthalamic adhesion (massa intermedia)  
- Lateral surface: separated from lentiform nucleus by the internal capsule  

**4. Site, afferent, efferent, and function of anterior thalamic nuclei**  
- Site: between the two limbs of Y‑shaped internal medullary lamina  
- Afferent: mammillothalamic fibres  
- Efferent: anterior thalamic radiation to cingulate gyrus  
- Function: part of limbic system (Papez circuit); concerned with recent memory and emotions  

**5. Afferent, efferent, and function of medial thalamic nuclei**  
- Afferent: hypothalamus, amygdala, olfactory cortex  
- Efferent: via medial forebrain bundle to prefrontal cortex  
- Function: part of limbic system; responsible for thinking and mood  

**6. Afferent, efferent, and names of the dorsal tier of lateral nuclei**  
- Afferent: receive input from other thalamic nuclei; multisensory integration  
- Efferent: sensory association areas of the cerebral cortex  
- Nuclei: lateral dorsal, lateral posterior, pulvinar  

**7. Mention afferent and efferent connections of the following nuclei**  
- **Ventral lateral (VL) & ventral intermediate (VI):**  
  - Afferent from cerebellum → efferent to premotor and motor areas (motor planning)  
- **Ventral anterior (VA):**  
  - Afferent from basal ganglia → efferent to supplementary motor area  
- **Ventral posteromedial (VPM):**  
  - Afferent from trigeminal lemniscus → efferent to lower one‑third of sensory cortex  
- **Ventral posterolateral (VPL):**  
  - Afferent from medial and spinal lemnisci → efferent to upper two‑thirds of sensory cortex  

**8. Mention afferent and efferent connections of MGB and LGB**  
- Medial geniculate body: receives auditory input from inferior colliculus; projects auditory radiation to auditory cortex  
- Lateral geniculate body: receives visual input from optic tract; projects visual radiation to visual cortex  

**9. Describe afferent, efferent, and function of:**  
- **Midline nuclei:**  
  - Receive input from midbrain reticular formation; project diffusely to entire cortex; increase cortical activity; part of reticular activating system  
- **Reticular nucleus:**  
  - Receives input from entire cortex; projects to thalamic nuclei; inhibits thalamic activity during sleep  

**10. Describe blood supply of the thalamus**  
- **Arterial:**  
  - Medial and anterior regions – posteromedial group of posterior cerebral artery  
  - Lateral and posterior regions – posterolateral group (thalamogeniculate arteries)  
- **Venous:** Thalamostriate vein  

**11. Describe the site and extent of the hypothalamus**  
- Anterior: lamina terminalis  
- Posterior: vertical plane posterior to mammillary bodies  
- Superior: up to hypothalamic sulcus  
- Inferior: forms base of brain beneath the third ventricle (floor of interpeduncular fossa)  

**12. Mention parts of the hypothalamus**  
- Optic chiasma  
- Tuber cinereum  
- Mammillary bodies  

**13. Enumerate nuclei of the hypothalamus**  
- Suprachiasmatic  
- Supraoptic  
- Infundibular (arcuate)  
- Tuberal  
- Paraventricular  
- Mammillary nuclei  

**14. Mention functions of the hypothalamus**  
- Controls autonomic and endocrine functions  
- Regulates food intake, fluid balance, and body temperature  
- Controls emotions, reproduction, and biological clock  

**15. Describe connection of hypothalamus with prefrontal cortex**  
- Periventricular fibre system connects hypothalamus with dorsomedial nucleus of thalamus (bidirectional)  

**16. Describe connection of hypothalamus with limbic system**  
- Medial forebrain bundle connects brainstem central gray to hypothalamus, amygdala, and septal areas  
- Fornix connects hippocampus to mammillary bodies → thalamus (Papez circuit)  
- Stria terminalis carries afferents from amygdala to preoptic nucleus  

**17. Describe connection of hypothalamus with lower centres**  
- Midbrain tegmentum: mammillary peduncle (afferent) and mammillotegmental tract (efferent)  
- Posterior longitudinal fasciculus carries efferents to autonomic nuclei of brainstem and spinal cord (lateral horn cells)  

**18. Describe connection of hypothalamus with pituitary gland**  
- Hypothalamo‑hypophyseal tracts:  
  - Supraoptic‑hypophyseal (vasopressin)  
  - Paraventricular‑hypophyseal (oxytocin)  
- Infundibular (arcuate) nucleus secretes releasing and inhibiting hormones via hypophyseal portal system to anterior pituitary  

**19. Subthalamus lies between ……**  
- Thalamus and midbrain tegmentum  

**20. Pineal body lies inferior to ……; its base is formed of ……**  
- Inferior to splenium of corpus callosum  
- Base formed by superior lamina (habenular commissure) and inferior lamina (posterior commissure)  

**21. Describe function of habenular nuclei**  
- Receive olfactory input via habenular stria  
- Send output to brainstem visceral nuclei (salivatory, dorsal vagal, ambiguus) via fasciculus retroflexus  
- Responsible for visceral responses to smell  

**22. Mention nuclei of the posterior commissure**  
- Darkschwitsch nucleus  
- Interstitial nucleus of Cajal  

**23. Mention function of the posterior commissure**  
- Connects both superior colliculi  
- Connects both medial longitudinal fasciculi  
- Connects pretectal nuclei of both sides  

**24. Describe boundaries of the third ventricle**  
- Lateral: thalamus and hypothalamus  
- Roof: ependyma with tela choroidea; choroid plexus hangs as two longitudinal elevations  
- Floor: optic chiasma, infundibulum, tuber cinereum, mammillary bodies, posterior perforated substance, midbrain tegmentum  
- Anterior: lamina terminalis, columns of fornix, anterior commissure  
- Posterior: posterior commissure, pineal body, suprapineal recess  

**25. Mention recesses of the third ventricle**  
- Optic recess  
- Infundibular recess  
- Pineal recess  
- Suprapineal recess  

**26. Mention functions of the pineal gland**  
- Endocrine gland secreting melatonin  
- Inhibits pituitary, pancreas, adrenals, gonads, and parathyroids  
- After puberty becomes calcified forming brain sand (radiological landmark)  

---

# Limbic System

**1. Mention cortical structures of limbic system**  
- Limbic lobe  
- Septal area  
- Hippocampal formation  
- Prefrontal cortex  

**2. Mention subcortical structures of limbic system**  
- Hypothalamus  
- Anterior nucleus of thalamus  
- Amygdaloid nucleus  

**3. Mention connecting pathways in limbic system**  
- Fornix  
- Cingulum  
- Stria medullaris thalami  
- Stria terminalis  
- Medial forebrain bundle  

**4. Enumerate parts of limbic lobe**  
- Subcallosal area  
- Cingulate gyrus  
- Isthmus  
- Parahippocampal gyrus  
- Uncus  

**5. Write in brief connections of Papez circuit**  
- Cingulate gyrus receives signals from association areas and is connected to parahippocampal gyrus and uncus via cingulum  
- Parahippocampal gyrus connects to hippocampus  
- Hippocampus connects to mammillary bodies via fornix  
- Mammillary bodies connect to anterior nucleus of thalamus via mammillothalamic tract  
- Anterior nucleus of thalamus projects to cingulate gyrus via anterior thalamic radiation  

**6. The anterior end of hippocampus is called ……, …… is a thin white matter layer beneath ventricular surface of hippocampus. These converge to form …… continuous with crus of fornix**  
- Pes hippocampi  
- Alveus  
- Fimbria  

**7. Crura of fornix come close near midline forming ……, behind it is …… which crosses the midline. Anteriorly it forms …… which end on mammillary bodies**  
- Body of fornix  
- Commissure of fornix  
- Columns of fornix  

**8. Mention functions and connections of septal areas**  
- Function: centre of pleasure  
- Connections:  
  - Medial forebrain bundle connects septal areas and amygdaloid nuclei to hypothalamus  
  - Stria medullaris thalami connects septal areas to habenular nuclei  

**9. Describe position of amygdaloid nucleus**  
- Located close to the tail of caudate nucleus, anterior to the hippocampus, related to the tip of the inferior horn of lateral ventricle  

**10. Describe result of the following:**  
- **a) Lesion of Papez circuit in chronic alcoholism**  
  - Anterograde amnesia  
- **b) Bilateral amygdalectomy**  
  - Docility  
  - Hyperphagia  
  - Increased sexuality

# Cerebral White Matter

**1. Superior longitudinal bundle connects ……, while inferior connects ……**  
- Superior longitudinal bundle: frontal lobe to occipital and temporal lobes  
- Inferior longitudinal bundle: temporal and occipital lobes  

**2. The bundle which connects Wernicke’s and Broca’s areas**  
- Uncinate bundle  

**3. Cingulum connects ……**  
- Cingulate gyrus to parahippocampal gyrus  

**4. Mention fibres passing in anterior limb and genu of internal capsule**  
- Anterior limb: frontopontine fibres and anterior thalamic radiation  
- Genu: corticonuclear fibres  

**5. Mention fibres passing in posterior limb of internal capsule**  
- Corticospinal fibres  
- Frontopontine fibres  
- Corticorubral fibres  
- Superior thalamic radiation (sensory radiation)  

**6. Mention contents of sublentiform and retrolentiform parts**  
- Sublentiform: auditory radiation, temporopontine and parietopontine fibres  
- Retrolentiform: optic radiation, parietopontine and occipitopontine fibres  

**7. Describe blood supply of internal capsule**  
- Upper half of anterior and posterior limbs: middle cerebral artery  
- Lower half of posterior limb: posterior communicating and anterior choroidal arteries  
- Genu and lower half of anterior limb: anterior cerebral artery  
- Retrolentiform and sublentiform parts: anterior choroidal artery  

**8. Describe relations of corpus callosum**  
- Superior: falx cerebri and anterior cerebral artery  
- Inferior: fornix and septum pellucidum  

**9. Rostrum of corpus callosum connects ……, while genu connects ……**  
- Rostrum: orbital surfaces of the two frontal lobes  
- Genu: medial and lateral surfaces of the two frontal lobes  

**10. Mention areas connected by body of corpus callosum**  
- Wide areas of cortex in parietal, temporal and occipital lobes  

**11. Describe relation of tapetum to lateral ventricle**  
- Forms roof and lateral wall of posterior horn of lateral ventricle  

**12. Forceps major is formed by ……, forceps minor is formed by ……**  
- Forceps major: splenium  
- Forceps minor: genu  

**13. Describe connections made by anterior commissure**  
- Splits into anterior bundle connecting anterior perforated substance  
- Posterior bundle connecting temporal gyri  

**14. Posterior commissure connects ……**  
- Right and left pretectal nuclei, superior colliculi and medial longitudinal bundles  

**15. Interventricular foramen is bounded anteriorly by …… and posteriorly by ……**  
- Column of fornix  
- Anterior end of thalamus  

**16. Describe bounds of body of lateral ventricle**  
- Roof: body of corpus callosum  
- Floor (lateral to medial): body of caudate nucleus, stria terminalis and thalamostriate vein, thalamus, body of fornix  
- Medial wall: septum pellucidum anteriorly; corpus callosum and fornix meet posteriorly  

**17. Describe bounds of anterior horn of lateral ventricle**  
- Roof: body of corpus callosum  
- Floor: rostrum of corpus callosum (medial) and head of caudate nucleus (lateral)  
- Anterior: genu of corpus callosum  
- Medial: septum pellucidum and anterior column of fornix  

**18. Describe bounds of posterior horn of lateral ventricle**  
- Roof and lateral wall: tapetum of corpus callosum  
- Lateral wall: optic radiation then inferior longitudinal bundle  
- Medial wall: bulb of posterior horn (forceps major fibres) and calcar avis formed by calcarine sulcus  

**19. Describe bounds of inferior horn of lateral ventricle**  
- Roof: tail of caudate nucleus (lateral) and stria terminalis (medial), ending anteriorly in amygdaloid nucleus  
- Floor (lateral to medial): collateral eminence, hippocampus, fimbria continuous with posterior column of fornix  

**20. The choroid fissure lies between …… in body of lateral ventricle, while in inferior horn it lies between ……**  
- Body: body of fornix and upper surface of thalamus  
- Inferior horn: stria terminalis and fimbria  

**21. Mention arteries of tela choroidea**  
- Anterior choroidal artery (from ICA)  
- Posterior choroidal artery (from posterior cerebral artery)  

**22. Mention bounds of tela choroidea**  
- Posterior: base of transverse cerebral fissure below splenium of corpus callosum  
- Anterior: apex reaches interventricular foramen of Monro  
- Lateral: invaginates choroid fissure pushing ependymal lining  
- Inferior: invaginates roof of third ventricle  

**23. Denticulate ligament is formed by ……**  
- Pia mater  

**24. …… is found over cerebellum while …… is found below it**  
- Cisterna ambiens  
- Cisterna magna  

**25. Cisterna pontis contains ……, while interpeduncular cistern contains ……**  
- Basilar artery  
- Circle of Willis  

**26. Total volume of CSF is about ……, and …… are secreted daily**  
- 130–150 ml  
- 300 ml  

**27. Mention functions of CSF**  
- Protection of brain against trauma (water jacket)  
- Helps maintain constant intracranial volume  
- Removal of neuronal metabolites  

**28. Describe course of vertebral artery**  
- Arises from first part of subclavian artery  
- First part: before foramen transversarium  
- Second part: passes through transverse foramina of upper six cervical vertebrae  
- Third part: in suboccipital triangle, enters cranial cavity via foramen magnum  
- Fourth part: runs on ventral surface of medulla  
- Ends at lower border of pons by joining opposite vertebral artery to form basilar artery  

**29. Mention branches of vertebral artery in cranial cavity**  
- Meningeal branches  
- Posterior inferior cerebellar artery  
- Anterior and posterior spinal arteries  
- Medullary branches  

**30. Mention branches of basilar artery**  
- Pontine arteries  
- Labyrinthine artery  
- Anterior inferior cerebellar artery  
- Superior cerebellar artery  
- Posterior cerebral artery  

**31. Mention arteries forming circle of Willis**  
- Right and left anterior cerebral arteries joined by anterior communicating artery  
- Right and left internal carotid arteries  
- Right and left posterior cerebral arteries  
- Posterior communicating arteries connecting ICA and PCA  

**32. Mention central branches of circulus arteriosus and their supply**  
- Anteromedial group (from ACA): caudate and anterior part of lentiform nucleus, parts of internal capsule  
- Anterolateral group (from MCA): caudate and posterior part of lentiform nucleus, parts of internal capsule  
- Largest branch: Charcot’s artery (artery of cerebral haemorrhage)  
- Posteromedial group (from PCA): anterior and medial thalamic nuclei and hypothalamus  
- Posterolateral group (from PCA): lateral and posterior thalamus and metathalamus  
- Largest branch: thalamogeniculate artery  

**33. Mention cortical supply of anterior cerebral artery**  
- Medial surface except occipital lobe  
- Upper one‑inch strip of lateral surface  
- Medial part of orbital gyrus  

**34. Describe supply and lesion of anterior cerebral artery**  
- Supplies motor and sensory areas of contralateral lower limb  
- Thrombosis of congenitally unpaired ACA causes cerebral paraplegia  

**35. Mention cortical areas supplied by middle cerebral artery, functional supply and lesion**  
- Supplies lateral surface except areas of ACA and PCA  
- Supplies lateral orbital surface and temporal pole  
- Functionally supplies motor and sensory areas of upper limb, speech and auditory areas, frontal eye field  
- Thrombosis is severe; lesion of dominant side causes aphasia  

**36. Mention cortical areas supplied by posterior cerebral artery, functional supply and lesion**  
- Supplies entire occipital lobe  
- Lower border strip of lateral surface  
- Inferior (tentorial) surface except temporal pole  
- Supplies visual cortex of contralateral visual field  
- Occlusion causes homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing due to MCA anastomosis  

**37. Describe superficial system of cerebral veins**  
- Superior cerebral veins drain into superior sagittal sinus  
- Superficial middle cerebral vein drains into cavernous sinus and communicates with superior sagittal and transverse sinuses  
- Deep middle cerebral vein drains insula and joins anterior cerebral and striate veins to form basal vein draining into great cerebral vein  
- Inferior cerebral veins drain into nearby sinuses, mainly transverse sinus  

**38. Thalamostriate vein drains into ……, which unites with the opposite side to form ……, which forms …… by uniting with ……**  
- Internal cerebral vein  
- Great cerebral vein  
- Straight sinus  
- Inferior sagittal sinus

# Embryology

**1. Mention sources of mesenchymal core of pharyngeal arches**  
- Paraxial mesoderm which forms musculature  
- Migrating neural crest cells which form skeletal elements or arch cartilage  

**2. Internal grooves of pharyngeal arches are called……, while external are called……**  
- Internal: Pharyngeal pouches  
- External: Pharyngeal clefts  

**3. Mention structures invading each pharyngeal arch**  
- An aortic arch connecting aortic sac with corresponding dorsal aorta  
- A cranial nerve from the adjacent hindbrain  

**4. 1st arch divides into 2 prominences which are……**  
- Ventral mandibular prominence  
- Dorsal maxillary prominence  

**5. Mention derivatives of 1st pharyngeal arch**  
- Skeletal elements form two cartilages: Meckel’s ventral cartilage and dorsal cartilage in maxillary prominence; both disappear leaving incus and malleus near the developing ear  
- Mesenchymal elements around Meckel’s cartilage give mandible by membranous ossification, sphenomandibular ligament, spine of sphenoid, and anterior ligament of malleus  
- Mesenchyme in maxillary process gives maxilla, zygomatic bone, palatine, and squamous temporal bones by membranous ossification  
- Gives all muscles supplied by mandibular branch of trigeminal nerve and the nerve itself  
- Aortic arch forms the maxillary artery  

**6. Enumerate derivatives of the 2nd pharyngeal arch**  
- Reichert’s cartilage gives stapes, styloid process, stylohyoid ligament, lesser cornu, and upper part of body of hyoid  
- Gives all muscles supplied by facial nerve and the nerve itself  
- Stapedial artery  

**7. Mention derivatives of the 3rd pharyngeal arch**  
- Greater cornu and lower part of body of hyoid  
- Stylopharyngeus muscle and glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)  
- Common carotid artery and internal carotid artery; external carotid artery arises as a sprout  

**8. Mention derivatives of the 4th pharyngeal arch**  
- All laryngeal cartilages except cricoid and epiglottis  
- Cricothyroid, levator palati, and pharyngeal constrictor muscles  
- Superior laryngeal nerve of vagus  
- Arch of aorta on left; arch of subclavian artery on right  

**9. Mention derivatives of the 6th pharyngeal arch**  
- Cricoid cartilage  
- Laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid  
- Recurrent laryngeal nerve of vagus  
- Proximal parts on both sides form pulmonary arteries; distal part disappears on right and remains on left as ductus arteriosus  

**10. General reason for occurrence of 1st arch syndromes**  
- Due to insufficient migration of neural crest cells to the 1st pharyngeal arch  

**11. Describe the following syndromes**  
- **Treacher Collins syndrome**  
  - Autosomal dominant  
  - Underdeveloped zygomatic bone  
  - Defect of lower eyelids  
  - Deformed external ear  
- **Pierre Robin syndrome**  
  - Mandibular hypoplasia  
  - Eye and ear defects  
  - Cleft palate  

**12. Describe fate of 1st pharyngeal cleft**  
- Persists and forms the external auditory meatus and outer surface of tympanic membrane  
- Auricle develops from six hillocks around external auditory meatus which later fuse  

**13. The mesoderm of ….. proliferates and covers …… clefts till it fuses with ……., forming…… that later disappears**  
- Mesoderm of 2nd arch  
- Covers 2nd, 3rd, and 4th clefts  
- Fuses with ectodermal covering of 6th arch  
- Forms cervical sinus  

**14. Explain the following abnormalities**  
- **Preauricular cyst**  
  - Failure of fusion between hillocks of auricle  
- **Branchial cyst**  
  - Failure of obliteration of cervical sinus; may appear along anterior border of sternomastoid  
- **Branchial fistula**  
  - External: failure of fusion of 2nd and 6th arches  
  - Internal: rupture of cervical sinus into 2nd pouch communicating with pharynx  

**15. Mention derivatives of 1st pharyngeal pouch**  
- Tubotympanic recess  
- Distal part forms lining of tympanic cavity, mastoid antrum, and inner surface of tympanic membrane  
- Proximal part forms Eustachian tube  

**16. Mention derivatives of 2nd pharyngeal pouch**  
- Endodermal lining forms epithelial buds penetrating mesoderm forming epithelium of palatine tonsils  
- Invaded by lymphoid tissue in 5th–7th months  
- Remnant forms tonsillar fossa  
- Dorsal part may share in tubotympanic recess  

**17. Mention derivatives of 3rd pharyngeal pouch**  
- Distal part forms inferior parathyroid glands  
- Ventral part forms thymus gland which later descends  
- Thymus invaded by lymphoid tissue in 3rd intrauterine month  

**18. Mention derivatives of 4th pharyngeal pouch**  
- Dorsal part forms superior parathyroid glands  
- Ventral part forms a transient thymic component that disappears  

**19. Mention derivatives of 5th pharyngeal pouch**  
- Forms caudal pharyngeal complex  
- Gives ultimobranchial body  
- Forms parafollicular (C) cells producing calcitonin  

**20. Describe DiGeorge syndrome**  
- Failure of development of 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches  
- Absence of thymus and parathyroids  
- Deformed mouth and nasal clefts  
- Cardiovascular abnormalities  

**21. The olfactory placodes appear during……**  
- 5th week  

**22. Enumerate derivatives of the intermaxillary segment**  
- Labial component: philtrum of upper lip  
- Jaw component: part of upper jaw carrying four incisors  
- Palatal component: primary palate  

**23. There is a solid rod between maxillary prominence and lateral nasal prominence that later gives rise to……, that open into …..and expand cranially forming…..**  
- Nasolacrimal duct  
- Opens into lateral nasal wall  
- Expands cranially forming lacrimal sac  

**24. Lateral parts of upper lip are derived from…… while philtrum from……**  
- Lateral parts: maxillary prominences  
- Philtrum: frontonasal prominence  

**25. Maxillary and mandibular prominences fuse from……**  
- Lateral to medial to decrease size of stomodeal fissure  

**26. Explain and describe the following abnormalities**  
- **Oblique facial cleft**  
  - Failure of fusion between maxillary prominence and lateral nasal prominence  
  - Lacrimal duct persists as open furrow, often with cleft lip  
- **Macro‑ or microstomia**  
  - Over‑ or under‑fusion of maxillary and mandibular prominences  
- **Rare midline anomalies**  
  - Median cleft lip, cleft lower jaw, cleft nose  
  - More common minor forms: cleft chin and micrognathia  

**27. Development of CNS begins in……**  
- 3rd week  

**28. Mention parts of neuroectoderm and their derivatives**  
- Neural plate: brain, spinal cord, motor neurons, preganglionic autonomic fibres  
- Neural crest: parts of PNS, sensory neurons and ganglia, autonomic ganglia, postganglionic nerves  
- Ectodermal placodes: sensory ganglia of cranial nerves, parts of sense organs (lens of eye, inner ear)  

**29. …… triggers formation of neural plate**  
- Notochord  

**30. Raised edges of neural plate form…… then it invaginates forming……**  
- Neural folds  
- Neural groove  

**31. Anterior neuropore closes in…… while posterior in……**  
- Anterior: 25th day  
- Posterior: 27th day  

**32. Cranial parts of neural folds expand forming……, its cavity forms……, while caudal narrow part forms…… and its cavity forms……**  
- Forms three brain vesicles  
- Cavities form brain ventricles  
- Caudal part forms spinal cord  
- Cavity forms central canal  

**33. Neuroepithelial cells differentiate into……**  
- Neuroblasts  
- Glioblasts  
- Ependymal cells  

**34. Mention layers of neural tube and their derivatives**  
- Inner ependymal (germinal) zone: lining of central canal and ventricles  
- Intermediate mantle zone: grey matter  
- Outer marginal zone: white matter  

**35. Mention stages of neuroblast development**  
- With central process extending to lumen  
- Apolar  
- Bipolar  
- Multipolar  

**36. Describe embryology of myelination**  
- Starts in 4th month of intrauterine life  
- Not completed until 2nd year after birth  
- Motor fibres myelinate before sensory  
- Oligodendroglia in CNS and Schwann cells in PNS  

**37. Derivatives of spongioblasts are……**  
- Astrocytes  
- Oligodendroglia  

**38. The sites for crossing of commissural fibres between right and left are……**  
- Ventral lamina  
- Dorsal lamina  

**39. In neural tube, …… contains sensory neurons while …… contains motor neurons, separated by ……**  
- Dorsolateral (alar) lamina: sensory  
- Ventrolateral (basal) lamina: motor  
- Sulcus limitans  

**40. General reason for formation of cervical and lumbar enlargements of spinal cord**  
- Accumulation of nerve cells supplying the limb buds  

**41. Neurons opposite sulcus limitans in spinal cord develop into……**  
- Lateral horn in thoracolumbar region (sympathetic)  
- Lateral horn in sacral region (parasympathetic)  

**42. General reason for formation of posteromedian sulcus and anteromedian fissure**  
- Posteromedian sulcus: occlusion of dorsal part of central canal  
- Anteromedian fissure: bulging of two basal laminae more than floor plate  

**43. During……, the spinal cord fills the vertebral column; at birth it ends at…… while in adults it ends at……**  
- 3rd month: fills vertebral column  
- At birth: opposite L3 vertebra  
- In adults: opposite upper border of L2 vertebra  

**44. Spina bifida is most common in segments……, its most common cystic type is……**  
- L5–S1  
- Meningomyelocele  

**45. Rachischisis of brain is called……, can be detected by……**  
- Anencephaly  
- Increased alpha‑fetoprotein during amniocentesis  

**46. Mention the two earliest flexures in brain development and describe them**  
- Cephalic flexure: between forebrain and midbrain  
- Cervical flexure: between hindbrain and spinal cord  
- Both are ventrally concave  

**47. Pontine flexure forms……, it differs from the previous ones by……**  
- Forms the 4th ventricle  
- Convexity is forward and it does not affect head shape  

**48. Mention developmental changes that occur to rhombencephalon**  
- Cavity dilates forming 4th ventricle  
- Lateral walls rotate like opening a book  
- Basal lamina becomes medial and alar lamina lateral  
- Remnants of sulcus limitans seen in floor of 4th ventricle  

**49. Mention derivatives of basal lamina**  
- Motor nuclei arranged in three columns:  
  1. General visceral efferent (parasympathetic)  
  2. Special visceral efferent (pharyngeal arches)  
  3. General somatic efferent (myotomes)
